title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative:
In February 2021, the new Turkey chapter of the Regional Refugee and Resilience Plan (3RP) was published by the 3RP Partners and launched with the Government of Turkey. It reflects refugees’ and host communities’ needs in Turkey focusing on protection, basic needs, education, health, food security and agriculture as well as livelihoods. The 3RP serves as a strategic guidance document for the operations of international community targeting Syrians and host communities in Turkey and is a resource mobilization tool at the same time. The international community supports the Government’s efforts through the Turkey Chapter of the 3RP. The 3RP combines a humanitarian response with longer-term interventions bolstering the resilience of refugees and host communities, while also capacitating national systems. It has been prepared and launched in close consultation between the Government of Turkey and 3RP partners. In Turkey, the plan aims for 3RP partners to work under the direction of the Government of Turkey to achieve better outcomes for Syrians under temporary protection and host communities alike. In addition, 3RP partners in Turkey established a task team on transition to employment with the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies/ Turkish Red Crescent Society (IFRC/TRC). As an outcome, a paper including good practices, lessons learned and recommendations has been developped.
Further, the coordination between the public institutions including the Director General International Labour Force and Director General of Migration Management mandated for migration management has been increased and together the two institutions have made administrative processes easier to access employment opportunities outside provinces where Syrian refugees are registered and the process of relocation to other cities now takes less time. As a 3RP member, the ILO contributed to the drafting of the new 3RP chapter, especially the section on livelihoods, ensuring that international labour standards are mainstreamed, decent work is promoted and transition to formal work supported. Further, the ILO actively contributed to the work of the task team on transition to employment and cooperation with the private sector to support transition to the formal labour market. The ILO promoted the compliance with ILS as well as transition to formality through its designed activities. The ILO capacity building activities targeting the social partners were noted in the 3RP as good practices. The Governments of Germany and United States and the European Union supported these activities.

title.narrative: 7.5.1. Number of member States with labour migration frameworks or institutional mechanisms to protect the labour rights of migrant workers and promote coherence with employment, skills, social protection, and other relevant policies
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative:
Technical capacity support was provided to labour market governance institutions on compliance with ILS and national legislation and on monitoring mechanisms supporting the integration of refugees into the Turkish labour market in line with economic, sectorial and regional priorities of Turkey. Social Security Auditors (SSI) and the labour inspectors have increased capacity to support employers that are informally employing refugees. The SSI auditors and the labour inspectors are able to guide employers on how to apply for work permit for refugee workers. Once any of the SSI auditors and the labour inspectors encounter migrants with an irregular status during the inspection process, they are better informed on how to proceed with the Ministry of Interior, Director General for Migration Management by taking into account the best interest of the refugee to enable them and their employers to secure their work permits.
A cooperation protocol with Justice Academy was signed in 2020 to carry out capacity strengthening training towards Labour Court Judges to increase the capacity of judges on labour migration, human rights, formal work of refugees and to provide exchange of knowledge and experience among judges and inspection/audit personnel of the Government. The overall objective the training towards Labour Court Judges was to increase awareness on the right to work for refugees in international and national contexts. Another aim was also bringing the Labour Court judges together to share law case experiences and increase the know-how transfer based on these law cases. The cooperation between the Director General for International Labour Force (DGILF) and Justice Academy has been started through the training activities. The information exchange among these institutions will improve the services provided to refugees and ensure they are in their best interest. The DGILF is often consulted by the Labour Courts for advisory purposes to close court cases. ILO has supported capacity strengthening training for Social Security Auditors, Experts of Social Security Institution (SSI) and the Labour Inspectors were provided in 2020 and 2021, delivered both face-to-face and online. As of August 2021, with US Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration (USBPRM) funding, 36 Social Security Auditors (SSI) Experts (9 female and 27 male) have attended an online training and 50 Social Security Auditors (36 male and 14 female) attended face-to-face training. The training consisted of: legislative status of refugees (Syrians and non-Syrians) in Turkey, their right to apply work permit and its procedures, refugees’ social security and labour market status in Turkey; COVID -19 effect on the world of work and social protection topics were also studied. Representatives from the Director General for International Labour Force and the Director General for Migration Management were present and intervened during the training. A team of trainers has been established in 2021, in the Justice Academy to carry out series of training towards Labour Court Judges. The cadre consist of 10 Supreme Court and Labour Court Judges. The Training of Trainers (ToT) was delivered in 2021 and the series of training will be carried out in the fall 2021. Through European Union funding, a tailor-made training on law enforcement and compliance targeting Labour Inspector Board Inspectors was delivered by ITC ILO in Turkey in February 2020. The program designed and implemented as a Training of Trainers session and included important topics such as Basic Principles and Rights at Work, Strategic Planning, Non-Standard Forms of Work and Working Conditions, and Psycho-Social Risks. This was an important step for the sustainability of the activities, as the modules contributed to the in-service training programs of the Guidance and Inspection Board.
